Alice — thanks for the clear asks. High level we can do a bounded inspection approach (sample sets + timebox) which should address your legal and Ops concerns and keep production blast radius low. Quick plan below — attaching a draft assurance addendum (redwood-assurance-addendum-draft.docx) with the proposed language we'd like legal to accept.

Proposed (summary):
- Evidence cadence: monthly automated artifact bundle (system config, identity lists, summary logs) + on-demand sample request with 48-72h SLA for delivery of redacted samples. Critical artifacts (SOC 2 report, major config diagrams) provided within 5 business days.
- Pen test: two candidate windows — preferred week of 2027-11-13, fallback window the week of 2027-12-04. Redwood will enable ephemeral staging credentials for external testers; testing will be restricted to non-production tenants unless explicitly agreed.
- Inspection boundary: bounded inspection clause limiting production access to scoped data sets, sampled evidence only, and explicit escalation path for privileged requests.

Next steps we'd like from MediCore: confirm which of the two pen-test windows work, provide primary secops contact (you suggested secops@medicore.com), and mark any questions in the attached questionnaire that require deeper Ops input.

Marissa — looping you for any commercial impacts if we need an SLA exception or a one-time audit credit. Karthik — flagging for legal language; I attached the draft addendum with inline comments.

Thanks,

Forwarding Alice's confirmation and the questions — Hannah, Marissa, noted below are the legal redline positions we'd propose to move MediCore toward sign-off. I'm keeping these compact so procurement can re-run with legal quickly.

(Forwarded message quoted below for context)

--- Suggested redline language (high level) ---
1) Audit rights (limited): Redwood will provide documentary evidence and sample artifacts as set out in Exhibit A. On-site inspections will be replaced by a bounded inspection process: predefined sample sets exchanged in a secure repository and a 5-business-day evidence SLA.

2) Penetration testing: Customer may coordinate testing through an agreed third-party vendor. Testing is permitted only within a mutually agreed staging environment; Redwood will provide ephemeral credentials and will coordinate a blast-radius review. Any active scanning of Redwood-managed production services is prohibited unless a separate Service Arrangement is approved in writing. Pen test windows will be scheduled with 10 business days' notice and a mutually agreed fallback window.

3) Log retention & KMS: Redwood will retain authentication and access logs for a minimum of 12 months in hot storage and 24 months in archival storage. Redwood uses provider-managed keys for Hosted customers; customer-managed keys are available for Private deployments and Dedicated offerings per the Order Form appendix.

4) Evidence & redaction: Redwood will supply redacted samples where necessary to protect customer/third-party PII and will provide an evidence manifest listing available artifacts. Sensitive items may be redacted and replaced with certified statements of compliance.

5) Escalation & operations contact: For any time-bound evidence requests exceeding the SLA, the parties will escalate to designated security contacts (Redwood: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com; Customer: secops@medicore.com).

Commercial note to Marissa: If MediCore requires an on-site inspection exception or expanded production testing rights, we should surface a one-time audit credit and an SLR surcharge.

Hannah — if that language looks good I will insert the snippets into Exhibit A and produce a clean redline for their counsel. Also attaching a short pen-test scope spreadsheet I prepared (pen-test-scope-proposal.xlsx) that maps scanner/noise restrictions and sample endpoints.

Karthik Iyer
